proof_checks.reason: A common nonempty selected episode set, the same available order rank, common query floor, and h=0 are explicitly fixed. No stochastic assumptions are needed for these finite-array results. They do not provide a comparison after changing either selected set or a coverage guarantee.

C_B is monotone and 1-Lipschitz and commutes with finite order statistics. A_i and T_i are >=B since native and translated windows include h=0. Coordinate bounds therefore give |F-K|<=d_abs, |S-K|<=d_signed and their triangle bound, retaining ties.

For a common candidate universe and fixed count, choosing the m smallest signed distances minimizes their maximum. The manuscript correctly declines to infer minimization of the absolute-anchor radius, sum of radii, actual report gap, multivariate distance, or realized/expected pinball loss.

g_i(z)=max(z+u_i,-z+v_i)-|z| has the stated two branches, is 2-Lipschitz and lies in [min(u_i,v_i),max(u_i,v_i)]. Applying both coordinate bounds and same-rank stability validates max_i min(2|x-N_i|,|u_i-v_i|). Plateau conditions are sufficient only, and same-rank R>=F,S yields no loss ordering.

Both B_i<=B and B_i>=B orderings follow coordinatewise. Alternating H1 n720 t721 construction has 360 translated peaks c and 360 of 3c, corrected rank685, F=K=c and S=3c; all labels mature. Declining history t=H+n-1 makes all G=0 and raw headroom Hd, with opposite loss orderings under two future continuations. The (0,-4,-1,2) H1 illustration gives G=(4,0,1), translated peaks (2,5,5), rank3 and F6/S5/K4.

With the same fixed c,phi and historical residuals, recursion differences give M_i,h=N_i+h+phi^h(x-N_i). Reverse triangle and max stability give the stated peak bound. For 0<=phi<=1 coefficient=1-phi^H, with h=0 coefficient0. The text distinguishes algebra from an innovation law or predictive improvement.

The exact empirical pinball subgradient criterion is F_n(c-)<=tau<=F_n(c). For integer W*tau=j with 0<tau<1 the minimizer set is [G_(j),G_(j+1)], permitting duplicates; noninteger W*tau selects G_(ceil(W*tau)). Common positive scaling and current-floor translation preserve this set. Thus corrected F is not generally non-ERM.

J_m(a)=aU_m+(1-a)V_m is an affine fixed-report empirical preference objective on common origins. Componentwise dominance implies weak preference for all nonnegative weights; opposing signs give one interior crossing. Changing a does not refit another quantile, imply dominance over all consistent .95 scores, establish observed costs, supply an unbiased selector, establish independence or produce a confidence set.

The producer uses exact pair crossings and midpoint orderings and retains separate boundary/endpoint ties; the independent half-space calculation recovers all closed feasible minimizer intervals, including point-only methods. a=0/1 are limiting component objectives; finite positive omega=a/(1-a) requires interior a.
